name: ChatGPT
tagline: General-purpose conversational AI assistant for writing, coding, and research.
definition: ChatGPT is a conversational AI system that answers questions, drafts content, and helps with reasoning and coding tasks inside a browser or app. For many professionals it is the default place to test a new idea, summarize a document, or start a task before moving to a more specialized tool.
why_it_matters: It created the mainstream AI workbench for busy teams, moving from a novelty to a daily production tool in a matter of months. The product matters because it is fast to learn, broadly familiar, and often the first AI surface an organization tests for drafting, research, and code assistance.
workplace_use_cases: Drafting client-ready emails, updates, and executive summaries
Brainstorming product ideas, meeting agendas, and first-pass research notes
Reviewing rough code or explaining technical bugs in plain English
how_to_use: Open the app, choose a model, paste in context or a file, and ask for a specific outcome such as a summary, an email draft, or a technical explanation. Follow up with tighter prompts to refine tone, challenge assumptions, and turn the first pass into something you would actually send.
key_features: Natural-language chat with file upload support

pricing.free_tier_details: Free usage is limited by message caps and model access varies by plan and demand.

paid_plans.name: Plus
paid_plans.notes: Higher usage limits and faster access to new features.

paid_plans.name: Team
paid_plans.notes: Shared workspaces, admin controls, and collaboration tools.

logo_source_note: OpenAI public product mark used as a text-safe fallback; no third-party logo asset is bundled.

example_prompts.label: Meeting brief
example_prompts.text: Summarize this product meeting transcript into a one-page decision brief with risks, owners, and next steps.

example_prompts.label: Email rewrite
example_prompts.text: Rewrite this draft in a more concise and executive-friendly tone without losing the key technical details.

name: Claude
tagline: High-context assistant for writing, analysis, and long-form reasoning.
definition: Claude is a large-language-model assistant tuned for careful reasoning, long context windows, and writing tasks that need nuance. It is often chosen when organizations want a model that reads a lot of material at once and then produces a well-structured answer without flattening the source material.
why_it_matters: The model became important because it performs especially well on long documents, policy-heavy writing, and thoughtful synthesis. In professional settings, that matters when the output has to be clear, accurate, and readable enough to pass a stakeholder review without a full rewrite.
workplace_use_cases: Reading long proposals or policy documents and surfacing the key risks
Drafting nuanced client communications with a more natural tone
Summarizing technical notes and turning them into actionable next steps
how_to_use: Start with a project brief, paste in a long document or transcript, and ask for a summary, rewrite, or review with explicit constraints. Because Claude excels at long context, it works particularly well when you need the model to consider a lot of background before suggesting a next move.
key_features: Focused prompt workflows for research and editing

pricing.free_tier_details: Free usage includes a limited amount of messaging and access to smaller models; heavier usage is gated behind paid plans.

paid_plans.name: Pro
paid_plans.notes: Higher usage limits and more model access for individual professionals.

paid_plans.name: Team
paid_plans.notes: Shared workspace and usage controls for teams.

logo_source_note: Anthropic public product branding used for identification; the site keeps a text-based fallback when a logo asset is not shipped in-repo.

name: Gemini
tagline: AI assistant connected to Google Workspace, search, and multimodal workflows.
definition: Gemini is Google's conversational AI assistant for writing, analysis, search, and multimodal work across Google products. It is most useful when a team already lives in Google Workspace and wants AI support that can work with documents, images, and browser-style research in the same flow.
why_it_matters: Google's distribution gives it a large installed base inside enterprise and consumer workflows. The product matters because it sits directly alongside Gmail, Docs, and the broader Google ecosystem, which makes it a practical choice for organizations already standardizing on Google.
workplace_use_cases: Drafting and polishing content inside Google Workspace documents
Synthesizing notes from meetings, email threads, and research into a brief
Getting a faster first pass on research questions and image-based tasks
how_to_use: Open Gemini from the web or within Google Workspace, then ask for a specific deliverable such as a meeting summary, an outline, or a rewrite. It works best when you provide the source document or a clear set of constraints, because the quality depends on the context you feed it.
key_features: Multimodal input for text and images

pricing.free_tier_details: Free access includes a limited quota and access to a subset of models; higher limits and enterprise controls are paid features.

paid_plans.name: Google AI Pro
paid_plans.notes: Expanded usage limits and access to premium model tiers.

paid_plans.name: Google AI Ultra
paid_plans.notes: Higher usage caps and premium Google AI features for power users.

logo_source_note: Google public brand assets used for product recognition and direction; the site falls back to a text mark if the logo is not checked into the repo.

name: Perplexity
tagline: AI search assistant that answers with citations and references.
definition: Perplexity is a search-driven AI assistant designed to answer questions with cited sources instead of just generating text in the abstract. It is most useful when a professional wants a fast, source-backed answer and then wants to drill into the references behind it.
why_it_matters: Many teams use AI for research but struggle with hallucinated or weakly sourced answers. Perplexity stands out because it turns search into a structured assistant workflow, which makes it useful for competitive research, quick fact checking, and source-driven discovery.
workplace_use_cases: Getting cited answers to competitive and market questions
Scanning the latest commentary on an industry trend before a meeting
Turning a vague research prompt into a short, source-backed brief
how_to_use: Ask a direct research question, review the cited sources, and then follow up with a sharper question or ask for a comparison table. Use it for a rapid first pass on fact-finding, but always verify the underlying sources before citing the answer externally.

pricing.free_tier_details: Free users receive limited search volume and model access; paid tiers increase daily usage and advanced features.

paid_plans.name: Perplexity Pro
paid_plans.notes: Higher search limits and access to more advanced models.

paid_plans.name: Enterprise Pro
paid_plans.notes: Admin controls, security features, and managed deployment for teams.

logo_source_note: Perplexity public product branding used as a product label; no bundled logo asset is maintained in the repo.
